old.name: Gothic Quarter at dawn
old.label: WALLS
old.hook: 30 min · Plaça Reial → Catedral → Roman walls · before 09:00
old.text: 30 min · Plaça Reial → Catedral → Roman walls · before 09:00 Start at Plaça Reial (1848 neoclassical arcaded square, Gaudí's 1879 lamp posts), walk past the Patio de l'Hostal de Sant Antoni, up through Plaça Sant Felip Neri (Civil War bullet marks still visible on the church wall — 42 children killed here in a 1938 air raid), to the Catedral for the geese in the cloister (13, one per year of Santa Eulàlia's life). End at the Roman walls on Plaça Nova. Before 09:00 the streets are empty; by 10:00 the first tour groups arrive.

old.name: Sant Antoni → Raval → Boqueria
old.label: MARKET ROUTE
old.hook: 2h · three markets and the soul of central Barcelona
old.text: 2h · three markets and the soul of central Barcelona Begin at Mercat de Sant Antoni (1882 iron market reopened 2018) on a Sunday morning for the perimeter book market. Walk east via Carrer del Parlament (the vermut spine — Bar Calders, Varmuteo, Nostàlgic). Cross to Carrer de la Cera into El Raval : Rambla del Raval, Suculent, Bar Cañete on Carrer de la Unió. End at the Boqueria on La Rambla — go to the back of the market where the locals eat (Pinotxo, Bar Central).

old.name: Passeig de Gràcia Modernisme strip
old.label: MODERNISME
old.hook: From Plaça de Catalunya to Diagonal · the Quadrat d'Or in 1.5 km
old.text: From Plaça de Catalunya to Diagonal · the Quadrat d'Or in 1.5 km From Plaça de Catalunya, walk north on Passeig de Gràcia. Manzana de la Discordia at no. 35–43 (Casa Lleó i Morera, Casa Amatller, Casa Batlló — three different Modernista masters on one block); La Pedrera/Casa Milà at no. 92; cross to Carrer de Mallorca for the Sagrada Família. The best photographic light hits the west-facing façades between 15:00 and 17:00 in autumn.

walks:Park Güell from the back entrance.group: The hills and the pintxo street

old.name: Park Güell from the back entrance
old.label: PARK
old.hook: 1h30 · Carrer del Carmel approach · free zones first, Monumental Zone with timed ticket
old.text: 1h30 · Carrer del Carmel approach · free zones first, Monumental Zone with timed ticket Skip the queue at the official Carrer Olot entrance. Take the metro to Lesseps or El Carmel, then walk uphill via Carrer del Carmel. Enter through the high free zone — the pine forest, the viaducts, the panoramic terraces above the Monumental Zone. Descend with your timed ticket into the Hypostyle Hall and the trencadís terrace. Sunset (~20:00 summer) from the free upper zone is the canonical Barcelona postcard.

walks:Montjuïc heritage loop.group: The hills and the pintxo street

old.name: Montjuïc heritage loop
old.label: HERITAGE
old.hook: Half day · CaixaForum → Mies → MNAC → Miró → Olympic Stadium
old.text: Half day · CaixaForum → Mies → MNAC → Miró → Olympic Stadium From Plaça d'Espanya: CaixaForum (in Puig i Cadafalch's 1911 Casaramona textile factory, €6); Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (the 1929 Barcelona Pavilion, reconstructed 1986, €12); MNAC (Romanesque rooms — the destination); Fundació Joan Miró (Josep Lluís Sert 1975, €17); the Olympic Stadium 1992. The Magic Fountain free show runs Thu–Sun evenings in summer (21:00 onwards).

walks:Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl.group: The hills and the pintxo street

old.name: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl
old.label: PINTXOS
old.hook: Poble Sec · a dozen bars in 200 m · €1.50–2 per skewer
old.text: Poble Sec · a dozen bars in 200 m · €1.50–2 per skewer The 200-metre pedestrian street of Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec is lined with pintxos bars where Basque-style snacks are pinned with toothpicks on the counter. Pick what you want; pay per toothpick at the end (€1.50–€2). Wash down with vermut or txakoli. Best 19:30–21:30 — late afternoon to early evening, the local-density window.

calas:Sant Sebastià.group: The city sand, south to north

old.name: Sant Sebastià
old.hook: The oldest swimming on this coast and the locals' end — the southwest tip of the Barceloneta stretch, below the W hotel's glass sail. The Club Natació Barcelona keeps a saltwater pool and a winter-swimmers' tribe here, so you'll see grey-haired Catalans doing lengths in February while the tourists are three beaches up. Calmer sand, a real neighbourhood rhythm.
old.text: The oldest swimming on this coast and the locals' end — the southwest tip of the Barceloneta stretch, below the W hotel's glass sail. The Club Natació Barcelona keeps a saltwater pool and a winter-swimmers' tribe here, so you'll see grey-haired Catalans doing lengths in February while the tourists are three beaches up. Calmer sand, a real neighbourhood rhythm. Heads up — Still a city beach: the W-hotel end draws a polished crowd and beach-club prices, and the sand is the same imported, trucked-in fill as the rest. Not a cove. Open in Google Maps →

calas:Barceloneta.group: The city sand, south to north

old.name: Barceloneta
old.hook: The postcard one, and the most honest history on the shore: this sand was laid over the Somorrostro, a seafront shantytown of some 15,000 people razed in 1966 for a Franco naval review — the birthplace of flamenco dancer Carmen Amaya. Today it's chiringuitos, paella touts, a Frank Gehry fish sculpture catching the light, and bodies packed rail-to-rail in August.
old.text: The postcard one, and the most honest history on the shore: this sand was laid over the Somorrostro, a seafront shantytown of some 15,000 people razed in 1966 for a Franco naval review — the birthplace of flamenco dancer Carmen Amaya. Today it's chiringuitos, paella touts, a Frank Gehry fish sculpture catching the light, and bodies packed rail-to-rail in August. Heads up — The busiest and most worked-over strip in the city — pickpockets, hawkers selling warm beer and sarongs, and water that turns murky after a summer storm. Come for the spectacle, not the swim. Open in Google Maps →

calas:Bogatell.group: The city sand, south to north

old.name: Bogatell
old.hook: Walk northeast and the average age climbs and the noise drops — Bogatell is where Barcelona goes to actually read a book. Wide, well-raked sand, a volleyball-and-skate energy at the edges, and a breakwater that keeps the water steadier than the beaches downcoast. The local pick for a city swim that doesn't feel like a turnstile.

Heads up — Less to eat and drink than Barceloneta, the same trucked-in sand the council replenishes by roughly 30,000 cubic metres a year against erosion, and zero shade — bring your own. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Nova Icària
old.hook: The first beach past the Port Olímpic, and the one families decamp to — flatter water, a gentler shelf, fewer touts than Barceloneta a ten-minute walk back. The 1992 Olympic village rises behind it, so the whole stretch was drawn from a blank sheet for the Games. The quietest of the genuinely central beaches.
old.text: The first beach past the Port Olímpic, and the one families decamp to — flatter water, a gentler shelf, fewer touts than Barceloneta a ten-minute walk back. The 1992 Olympic village rises behind it, so the whole stretch was drawn from a blank sheet for the Games. The quietest of the genuinely central beaches. Heads up — Quiet is relative — it still fills on a July Sunday, and the backdrop is residential blocks and the twin Olympic towers, not cliffs and pine. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Mar Bella
old.hook: The free-spirited end: a long-standing place in the city's LGBTQ+ scene, a clearly marked clothing-optional stretch at its northern tip, a skate park and a sailing base behind. Of the central beaches this is the one that still feels like it belongs to people who live here rather than people photographing it.
